qa_pairs.question: What are the requirements to trade options?
qa_pairs.answer:
Currently, only margin accounts can trade options. If you only have a cash account, you can upgrade to a margin account in order to gain option trading capabilities.
Please be aware that a margin account must have a minimum $2,000 account balance (not including option positions) to place an options trade.
For example, if your account has $1,500 in cash and $1,000 in existing option contracts, you would
be able to place another option order because your account balance excluding option positions is under $2,000.

qa_pairs.question: Can I use margin to purchase option contracts?
qa_pairs.answer: Options are not marginable so you will not be able to use margin buying power to purchase option contracts.

qa_pairs.answer:

qa_pairs.question: When will the options trade settle?
qa_pairs.answer:
The settlement period for option transactions is T+1, which means it takes 1 business day for the trade to be settled.
For example, if you sell 2 contracts on Monday, the funds will be settled on Tuesday. (Provided both Monday and Tuesday are trading days.)

qa_pairs.question: What will happen to my contract on the expiration day?
qa_pairs.answer:
If the option contract is In-the-Money, we will examine your account and see if your account assets meet the contract obligation for either exercise or assignment. If so, the contract will be exercised or assigned after market closes. If not, we will force liquidate your positions for risk mitigation purposes.
If the option contract is Out-of-the-Money, the contract will expire worthless.
Please note: if you are selling a contract, you are always at the risk of being assigned. For risk control purposes, if you do not have sufficient assets to cover your upcoming exercise or assignment obligation, your option position might be force closed prior to market close on the expiration date.
If you are an option owner/buyer and holding an In-the-Money position on the expiration date, and decide not to exercise your option, please make sure to email:
to notify us no later than 5:00 P.M. EST of the expiration date.

qa_pairs.question: What are call options and put options?
qa_pairs.answer:
Call options
allow the holder to buy the asset at a stated price within a specific timeframe.
Put options
allow the holder to sell the asset at a stated price within a specific timeframe.

qa_pairs.question: What is the strike or exercise price?
qa_pairs.answer:
Each option contract will have a specific expiration date by which the holder must exercise their option. The stated price on an option is known as the
strike price
exercise price.
If you bought a call option, your call will be profitable if the market price of the stock goes above the strike price, since you can buy the stock at a price that is lower than the current market price. However, if the value of the stock stays below your strike price, your options contract will expire worthless.
Please note: You are not actually buying shares of the stock unless you exercise your contract. You are buying a contract that grants you rights to purchase stocks at a specific price on or before a certain date.

qa_pairs.question: What are Index Options?
qa_pairs.answer:
An Index option is an option contract that gives an investor the right to buy or sell the value of an underlying index at an exercise or strike price.
As opposed to equity options, Index options are cash settlement only. Investors will receive cash based on the difference between the exercised settlement value and the strike price rather than the delivery of underlying equity.
stock is being transferred, bought, or sold.
What are the fees associated with trading Index Options?
TradeUP currently does not charge any commission or fees for Index Options!
Order Types for trading Index Options
At TradeUP, currently only limit orders can be placed to trade Index Options.
TradeUP Index Option Hour Trading Hours:
Regular trading hours 9:30am - 4:00pm EST.
Exceptions: Index options NDX and NDXP trades from 9:30AM - 4:15pm EST.
Examples of Trading Index Options:
Cash Settled Call: If client purchases 50 XYZ cash-settled call index option and the reported exercise settlement value is $55.
The cash settlement value of the call option is $500. [(55-50) x 100 = $500].
Cash Settled Put: If client purchases 50 XYZ cash-settled put index option and the reported exercise settlement value of the put is $40.
The cash settlement value of the put option is $1,000 [(50-40) x 100 = $1,000].
Index Option Settlement:
Index options traded at TradeUP are all European Style Options.
European Style Options are options that can only be exercised on the designated expiration date.
A.M. Settlement - index options with A.M Settlement establishes their exercise settlement value 30 minutes after market opens on day of expiration.
AM Settled index options stop trading the day before expiration date.
PM Settlement - index options with PM Settlement establishes their exercise settlement value at market close on day of expiration.
PM Settled index options allow for trading of day of expiration up until market close.
If expiration date is non-trading day, it will be advanced to the previous trading day.
Exception is the non trading day is on Monday, then it will be postponed to the next Trading Day.

qa_pairs.question: How are my position value and P&L calculated?
qa_pairs.answer:
The market value, position profit/loss, and real-time risk control of options are uniformly calculated using the
Mark Price
. The daily profit/loss of options is calculated using the
Mark Price
and the
Previous Mark Price (Pre-mark)
General Rules for determining the Mark Price
When the last price lies between the best bid and best ask, the Mark Price is equal to the last price.
When the last price is not between the best bid and best ask or does not exist, the Mark Price is set to the mid-price (for single-leg option, mid-price generally equals to the average of the best bid and the best ask).
If the ask price does not exist and the last price is lower than the best bid, the Mark Price is set to the best bid.
If the ask price does not exist and the last price is higher than the best bid, the Mark Price is set to the last price.
If the bid price does not exist and the last price is lower than the best ask, the Mark Price is set to the last price.
If the bid price does not exist and the last price is higher than the best ask, the Mark Price is set to the best ask.
